key: At a Chennai railway booking counter
name: ch09_booking_clerk_handwriting
alt: A tired railway booking clerk at a Chennai counter smiles and sits taller after a passenger praises his beautiful handwriting on a reservation slip.
scene: A medium shot through the steel grille of a railway reservation counter in Chennai, mid-afternoon. On the LEFT, outside the window, a young man in his late twenties (light blue shirt, office lanyard, backpack) leans slightly towards the small speaking hole, pointing with one finger at a white reservation slip lying on the counter between them, his face warm and genuinely impressed. Behind him a short queue of three people all stare down at their phones, faces lit blue, nobody looking up. In the CENTRE, the slip is enlarged in a round inset bubble showing elegant flowing handwritten letters and a station code, with a small sparkle beside them. On the RIGHT, inside the booth, the clerk (about fifty, grey moustache, half-sleeve white shirt, reading glasses pushed up on his forehead, a tall stack of printed tickets and a rubber stamp beside him) has stopped mid-stamp, lifted his head and broken into a proud, surprised smile; a small thought bubble above him shows a father and a boy practising letters at a table under a lamp. A wall clock behind him reads four o'clock. A soft upward arrow rises beside the clerk to show him sitting a little taller. Warm afternoon light through a high window, gentle mood. Labels: "NOTICED" above the inset bubble of the slip, "400" small on the ticket stack.

key: Every family in India has a version
name: ch09_guest_is_god
alt: A family welcomes a visitor with the best chair, the first cup of chai and the fullest plate of sweets while a small child watches and copies.
scene: A warm interior view of a middle-class Indian living room in the evening, front-on like a stage. In the CENTRE sits the guest, a middle-aged man in a simple kurta, placed in the best chair of the house, a carved wooden armchair with a cushion, while everyone else perches on plastic chairs or the floor. On the LEFT, the mother of the house (forties, cotton sari, dupatta over shoulder) bends forward offering him the first cup of chai on a steel tray, steam curling from the glass, while a second cup waits behind on the tray. On the RIGHT, the father (fifties, half-sleeve shirt, spectacles) holds out a steel plate heaped with laddoos and barfi, clearly the fullest plate; a second smaller plate with only two sweets sits on a side table for the family. In the foreground, a small girl of about six in a frock watches from behind the sofa and, in imitation, carries a tiny glass of water towards the guest with both hands, tongue out in concentration. Thin dotted arrows run from the parents' hands to the child to show the habit being copied by watching. A framed family photo and a ceiling fan in the background, soft yellow tube-light glow. Labels: "GUEST" above the armchair, "FIRST CUP" beside the chai tray.

key: At a family wedding, two aunts both
name: ch09_two_aunts_two_counters
alt: At a wedding, the groom's mother gives one aunt charge of the sweets counter and the other charge of the main buffet, and both proudly run their own corner.
scene: A wide view of an outdoor Indian wedding dinner under a decorated shamiana at night, strings of marigold and small fairy lights along the top. The scene is split into two zones by a pillar wrapped in flowers. LEFT zone: a sweets counter with brass trays of laddoos, jalebis and gulab jamun; the first aunt (sixties, bright pink silk sari, big bindi, reading glasses on a chain) stands behind it, chin up, inspecting a laddoo between finger and thumb like a judge. RIGHT zone: the main buffet with steel chafing dishes and two young caterers in white uniforms and caps; the second aunt (fifties, green silk sari, hair in a bun with jasmine) points firmly at a dish, and the caterers nod eagerly. In the CENTRE foreground stands the groom's mother (fifties, maroon sari, gold necklace), arms open wide in two directions, one hand pointing to each aunt, smiling calmly; two short curved arrows sweep from her hands to each counter. Each aunt has a small gold crown badge floating above her head. Warm festive light, happy busy mood with guests blurred in the background. Labels: "SWEETS" above the left counter, "BUFFET" above the right counter.

key: Two customers at the same Bengaluru
name: ch09_darshini_wrong_dosa
alt: Two customers at a Bengaluru darshini get the wrong dosa; the one who shouts gets a plain swap, the one who asks kindly gets extra chutney and a smile.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves set at the same steel counter of a busy standing-only Bengaluru darshini in the morning, steaming tawa and a cook in a white vest and folded lungi behind the counter in each half. LEFT panel: a man in his thirties (formal shirt, ID card, phone in hand) leans over the counter with his mouth wide open, a jagged red speech bubble with a big exclamation mark bursting from him and pointing at a plain dosa on a steel plate; the cook behind the counter frowns, shoulders hunched, sliding a replacement plate across without looking up. RIGHT panel: a young woman (late twenties, kurta, tote bag) holds the same wrong plate politely with a small apologetic smile and one hand raised gently; her rounded white speech bubble shows a small smiling face. The cook in this half grins and adds an extra ladle of coconut chutney to her new masala dosa, and a small thought bubble above him shows her face with a tick, meaning he will remember her next week. Warm morning light, steam rising. Labels: "SHOUT" at the top of the left panel, "ASK" at the top of the right panel, "+ CHUTNEY" small beside the extra ladle.

key: A college student in Pune writes a
name: ch09_blog_post_maintainer
alt: A student in Pune writes a sincere blog post praising a library's design; the maintainer, buried in complaints, reads it and invites her to help.
scene: A split composition joined by a dashed arrow. LEFT side: a college hostel room in Pune at night, a young woman student (about twenty, oversized hoodie, hair tied up, spectacles) sits cross-legged on a bed with a laptop, surrounded by printed pages of code covered in hand-drawn notes and highlighter marks, clearly having studied deeply; her laptop screen shows a blog layout with a heading bar and a small heart icon. A dashed teal arrow carrying a paper-plane icon flies from her laptop across the picture to the right. RIGHT side: a home office, the maintainer (a woman in her thirties, short hair, cardigan, mug of tea) sits at a desk facing a monitor. Behind her monitor a tall pile of grey envelope icons with red exclamation badges represents bug reports and complaints. On the screen, the student's post glows warmly in amber against the grey pile. The maintainer leans in with a surprised, touched smile, one hand on her chest. A speech bubble from her reads only a small handshake icon and a version tag "v2". A faint time-arrow along the bottom edge leads to a tiny inset of the student two years later with a team badge. Soft lamplight on both sides. Labels: "STUDIED" above the student's notes, "BUG REPORTS" on the grey pile.

key: In a school cricket team in a small
name: ch09_coach_opening_bowler
alt: A school cricket coach tells a quiet long-off fielder he will open the bowling tomorrow, and the boy walks home transformed.
scene: A two-moment scene on a dusty small-town school cricket ground at late afternoon, a brick school building and a neem tree in the background. LEFT and CENTRE: the coach (forties, track suit, whistle round his neck, cap) stands beside the practice nets with one hand on the shoulder of a thin, quiet boy of about fourteen in white cricket clothes holding a red ball; the coach's other hand points towards the pitch, and a speech bubble from him shows a cricket ball with a curved swing arrow. The boy looks up wide-eyed and startled, mouth slightly open. A faint dotted trail of footprints leads from a far boundary flag, showing where he usually fields. RIGHT: the same boy walking home along the road outside the ground gate, school bag on his back, chest out, head high, a broad grin, one fist clenched; behind him a large faint translucent silhouette, much taller than he is, shows a bowler in mid-delivery, the player he now believes he can be. Small upward sparkle lines around him. Warm golden light, uplifting mood. Labels: "LONG-OFF" on the far boundary flag, "OPENING BOWLER" above the walking boy.

name: ch09_watchman_knows_all
alt: A young software engineer asks his building's watchman how he remembers every car and face, and the watchman lights up explaining.
scene: A front view of the main gate of a Gurugram apartment society in the early evening, a small watchman's cabin with a register, a plastic chair and a steel flask on the LEFT, the tall towers lit behind. The watchman (fifties, khaki uniform, beret cap, thick moustache, logbook under his arm) stands beside the cabin, one hand raised and counting on his fingers, face glowing with pride as he explains. Around his head float a ring of small round memory bubbles: a white hatchback with a number plate, a delivery rider with a helmet and a bag, a flat door with a padlock and a little suitcase icon for a family away on holiday, and a tower block marked with a letter. On the RIGHT, a young resident (late twenties, office backpack, laptop sleeve, lanyard) stands facing him with a genuinely curious, slightly amazed expression, eyebrows raised, hand open as if asking. Above the resident hangs a small thought bubble with a big question mark next to a tower icon, showing he does not know where his own neighbour lives. A graduation cap icon hangs faintly near the resident to hint at his degree. Warm streetlight just switching on, friendly mood. Labels: "HOW?" in the resident's speech bubble, "KNOWS ALL" above the watchman's memory ring.

key: At a family function, the grandmother
name: ch09_grandmother_brass_lamp
alt: At a family function, one grandson-in-law asks the grandmother about an old brass lamp and listens for forty minutes while the cousins stay on their phones.
scene: A wide interior view of a crowded Indian family function in a living room decorated with marigold strings. On the LEFT and in the background, a group of four cousins in their twenties stand in a tight circle, all looking at their phones or talking about jobs, backs half turned to the room. In the RIGHT corner, the grandmother (late seventies, white cotton sari with a thin border, spectacles, silver hair in a bun) sits on a low cane chair, animated now, one hand raised mid-story. On the wall above her hangs an old brass oil lamp with five wicks, catching the light. Sitting on a stool facing her, leaning forward with elbows on knees, is a grandson-in-law (early thirties, pale kurta, attentive listening face) who has just pointed up at the lamp. A large story bubble rises from the grandmother showing three small scenes in a row: a village wedding with a mandap, a mud-walled village house, and a smiling young husband holding the lamp. In her lap she holds out an old steel wristwatch towards the young man. A small wall clock between the two groups shows forty minutes passed with a curved arc. Two of the cousins glance over in surprise with small exclamation marks. Warm lamp-lit glow on the corner, cooler light on the phone group. Labels: "1962" small inside the story bubble, "LISTENING" above the grandson-in-law.

key: A plumber fixing a pipe in a retired
name: ch09_plumber_colonel_bonsai
alt: A plumber admires a retired colonel's balcony bonsai; the colonel forgets the leaking tap and gives him a jade plant for his daughter.
scene: A side view of a sunny balcony of a flat in Dehradun with hills faintly visible beyond the railing. Along the balcony railing on wooden shelves stand rows of bonsai trees in shallow ceramic pots, the largest a gnarled miniature banyan with aerial roots in a wide blue pot at the CENTRE. On the LEFT, a plumber (thirties, navy work shirt, toolbag over shoulder, wrench in hand) stands beside the banyan, bending slightly, pointing at it with an amazed open-mouthed expression. On the RIGHT, the retired colonel (seventies, white moustache, sleeveless sweater over a checked shirt, straight-backed) gestures proudly at the trees with one hand, beaming, clearly mid-tour. Behind them through the open balcony door, a kitchen tap drips slowly into a steel bucket with tiny drip lines, forgotten for now. In the colonel's other hand he holds a small jade plant in a terracotta pot, offering it towards the plumber; tucked against the pot is an envelope with handwritten lines on the back. A small dotted arrow loops from the plumber's pointing finger to the banyan and back to the gift. Bright morning light, gentle humour. Labels: "40 YEARS" on a small tag on the banyan pot, "FOR YOUR DAUGHTER" small on the envelope.

key: A furniture supplier meets the busy
name: ch09_teak_counter_supplier
alt: A furniture supplier skips his catalogue to admire a restaurant owner's teak bar counter, and the owner tells his story for an hour.
scene: An interior of a restaurant owner's office in Bengaluru, warm wood tones. At the CENTRE stretches a beautiful polished teak bar counter with carved edges and visible fine joinery, the grain glowing. On the LEFT, the furniture supplier (forties, rolled-sleeve formal shirt, spectacles) stands running his palm along the counter's edge, admiring it with real appreciation; under his other arm a thick closed catalogue sits unopened, with a small grey cross badge on it. On the RIGHT, the restaurant owner (fifties, crisp shirt, grey-streaked hair, a mobile phone face-down on the counter) leans back against the counter, animated, both hands moving as he tells a story. A large story bubble above him shows three small vignettes in a row: a modest roadside dhaba with a tin roof, a carpenter with a chisel and a mundu working the wood, and a bank passbook with a tick. A wall clock behind shows a curved arc of one hour passed. In the lower right corner a small inset shows the two men later seated at a restaurant table sharing a meal, and a paper order slip with a little chair drawing and a green tick. Golden late-morning light. Labels: "TEAK" on the counter front, "ORDER" on the order slip.

name: ch09_cook_sambar_praise
alt: At Sunday lunch, the father praises the family cook's sambar in front of all the relatives, and she decides to stay.
scene: A warm front view of a family Sunday lunch in a South Indian home, a long dining table covered with steel plates, banana-leaf portions of rice, and a big steel vessel of sambar at the CENTRE with steam curling up. Around the table sit relatives: an elderly uncle, a young cousin, and the mother (forties, cotton sari). At the head of the table, the father (fifties, white shirt and veshti) stands with one hand raised towards the kitchen doorway, speaking proudly to everyone, his face warm. On the RIGHT in the kitchen doorway stands the long-time cook (fifties, simple printed sari tucked at the waist, steel ladle in hand), surprised and touched, a hand at her cheek, a small blush. At her feet a cloth bag packed for the village sits half-zipped, a small bus ticket poking out, with a dashed fading line showing the plan to leave. Above the father's head a speech bubble contains a steaming sambar bowl with a gold star. In the top corner a small inset card shows a housewarming invitation with her name written on it. All relatives turn towards her, a couple clapping. Soft midday light through a window. Labels: "THANK YOU" above the cook, "SAMBAR" on the steel vessel.

key: Think of a good wedding photographer
name: ch09_wedding_photographer_stars
alt: A wedding photographer turns away from the couple to make the grandmother, the band uncle and the mehendi cousin each feel like the star.
scene: A lively wide view of an Indian wedding hall, a decorated mandap with flowers in the background where the couple sits small and slightly out of focus. In the foreground, the wedding photographer (thirties, black kurta, camera with a big lens, a second camera on a strap) moves across the picture from LEFT to RIGHT, and we see the three moments as one curved path of dotted footsteps. First, on the LEFT, the grandmother (eighties, silk sari, big spectacles) sits on a chair beaming shyly as the photographer kneels and snaps her, a tiny spotlight cone falling on her. In the CENTRE, an uncle (fifties, safari suit, moustache) proudly poses beside a big wedding dhol drum from the band he arranged, a spotlight cone on him too. On the RIGHT, a young cousin (twenties, lehenga) holds up her hands to show off the intricate mehendi patterns she painted on the bride, glowing under her own spotlight. A small star badge hangs above each of the three, and a tiny stopwatch icon beside each shows thirty seconds. Warm festive golden light, marigold garlands hanging from the top edge. Labels: "STAR" above the grandmother, "30 SEC" small near the stopwatch in the centre.

key: A good chaiwala outside a Bengaluru
name: ch09_chaiwala_six_ways
alt: A chaiwala outside a tech park smiles, remembers the order, uses the customer's name, asks about work and listens, so the customer walks past three other stalls to reach him.
scene: A street-level morning view outside a glass-fronted tech park in Bengaluru, a row of four small tea stalls along the footpath from LEFT to RIGHT. The first three stalls on the LEFT are plain and quiet, their sellers looking at phones, with small grey dashed arrows showing a young engineer walking straight past each of them. At the far RIGHT stands the favourite stall: a wooden cart with a steaming aluminium kettle, a row of small glasses and a jar of rusks. The chaiwala (forties, checked half-sleeve shirt, towel over his shoulder, warm wide smile) is pouring tea from a height into a glass and leaning forward to chat. Facing him, the young engineer (late twenties, hoodie, office ID card, laptop backpack, tired eyes brightening) takes the glass. Around the chaiwala float six tiny numbered icons in a gentle arc: a smile, a sugar cube with a minus sign, a name tag, a laptop with a rocket for the release, an ear for listening, and a sun for looking less tired. Morning sun rising behind the tech park, friendly mood. Labels: "LESS SUGAR" small on the glass, "REGULAR" above the chaiwala's cart.
